correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs the autonomous two-mark chain, its positive transition kernel, and the equilibrium renewal-age mixture. The DLMF equal-index Mellin formula is valid at all sufficiently large site indices; the finite-age correction is super-algebraically small and the gamma-ratio first-order term vanishes for complementary shifts. Fixed reset-site shifts yield the two opposite alpha*b/n corrections; positive tail comparison gives the if-and-only-if moment threshold. Tonelli and the exact Bessel ballistic moment give the alpha>3 second moment, with an alpha=3 spatial logarithm. The included script independently checks 90 finite-parameter identities or comparisons; numerical checks are not used to prove the infinite-lattice limits.

originality.rationale: The inspected full text of Acharya--Gupta establishes the conditional quantum walker and Pareto waiting law, but gives no exact infinite-lattice stationary power-tail coefficient, no first left/right asymmetry term, and no infinite-lattice third-moment threshold; its alpha=3 finite-lattice numerical saturation is inapplicable to that threshold. Singh--Górska--Sandev covers the generic renewal formula and the diffusive mean-square threshold, not the conditional two-tail quantum statement. DLMF covers the Mellin integral, which is explicitly credited as classical. No claim-level match was identified in the documented literature and statement-level comparisons; generic renewal-plus-Mellin derivability remains a recorded residual risk.
residual_risks: A broader uninspected theorem in the quantum-resetting literature may imply this explicit conditional-reset formula.
The gamma-ratio asymptotic is classical; new method is not claimed.
The source paper finite-size alpha=3 saturation may be valid for finite chains and cannot resolve the infinite-volume limit.

value.rationale: The exact spatial decay and directional skew are physically motivated by the source protocol that generates asymmetric quantum localization. They identify what reset bias does and does not affect at extreme sites, and settle the infinite-volume observable boundary: stationary occupation exists for alpha>1 but its variance only for alpha>3. The coefficient of the marginal logarithmic divergence enables mathematically meaningful comparisons with finite-lattice truncation, which the motivating 41-site simulation could not decide. The result is not merely a rephrased moment substitution; the first skew correction is a new structural property of the conditional two-site dynamics.
